# Kafka source console contract

Operation: SCF-KAFKA-MERCHANT-8F43-20261012. This adapter extends the original SF30 NDJSON workspace and dataset/merchant/release engine.

## Source and ownership

Native files: kafka/shared.py, contract.py, transport.py, model.py, httpd.py, managed.py, cli.py, cli.mjs. Customer UI: kafka/public/index.html, app.js, style.css. Packaging map: kafka/browser-assets.json. The existing NDJSON app adds named exports api, work, refresh, notify, consoleReady, renderMapping and is served unchanged at /ndjson-app.js; its stylesheet is /ndjson-style.css.

The Kafka workspace retains the original NDJSON workspace.json and workspace.sqlite, with additional Kafka tables in a separate private kafka.sqlite database and a private kafka-workspace.json marker containing {"schema":"stellar-forge.kafka-workspace.v1","id":"<UUID>"}. One original workspace writer lease owns capture, projection and native dataset operations. Open/list/binding do not contact a broker.

All existing /api/state, /api/source, /api/plan, /api/build, /api/query, /api/compare, /api/changes, /api/changes/download, /api/export, /api/dataset-export, /api/import and /api/merchant retain their original NDJSON contracts. Kafka adds the routes below. Local host/origin/private bearer rules are those of the original server. Every JSON body has an exact documented key set; optional fields are named below. Errors are {"error":"actionable message"} with HTTP 400; missing records return 404 and origin/auth failure 403.

## Common types

IDs and content hashes are lowercase 64-character SHA-256 strings unless a field is explicitly named operation or connection. An operation is caller-chosen, 1–128 characters [A-Za-z0-9._:-]. It is unique within its operation kind; reusing it returns the retained operation only when its original arguments match. Decimal offsets are canonical nonnegative strings in signed 64-bit range. Partitions are nonnegative JSON integers. Revision, record and byte counts are nonnegative JSON integers. All timestamps are UTC ISO-8601 strings. Full key, value and header bytes use canonical base64; null remains distinct from empty bytes.

### Client status

client = {"available":true,"pythonPackage":"confluent-kafka","version":"2.16.0","libraryVersion":"...","requirement":"confluent-kafka==2.16.0"}
When unavailable, available is false and version/libraryVersion are null; message explains how the original selected Python installs the declared requirement. This is an offline import check. Opening the console never initiates a network call.

### Connection configuration

config = {
  "schema":"stellar-forge.kafka-connection.v1",
  "label":"Goldsky downstream topic",
  "brokers":["broker.example:9092"],
  "topic":"events",
  "security":{
    "protocol":"SASL_SSL",
    "mechanism":"SCRAM-SHA-512",
    "usernameEnv":"KAFKA_USERNAME",
    "passwordEnv":"KAFKA_PASSWORD"
  },
  "requestTimeoutSeconds":30,
  "maxMessageBytes":10485760,
  "maxCaptureBytes":268435456,
  "maxCaptureRecords":1000000
}

Supported protocols: PLAINTEXT, SSL, SASL_PLAINTEXT, SASL_SSL. SASL mechanisms: PLAIN, SCRAM-SHA-256, SCRAM-SHA-512. Optional TLS references: caFileEnv, certificateFileEnv, keyFileEnv, keyPasswordEnv. TLS file references name environment variables containing private local file paths. Username/password/private key material never appears in saved configuration, API results, browser requests or exports. Unknown security keys and literal credential fields are rejected. Request timeout is 1–120 seconds; message bytes 1–16 MiB; capture bytes 1–256 MiB; records 1–1,000,000.

POST /api/kafka/connection
{"connection":"goldsky-main","expectedRevision":0,"operation":"save-main-1","config":config}
Creates revision 1. Later saves require exact current expectedRevision. Result:
{"id":"goldsky-main","revision":1,"sha256":"...","operation":"save-main-1","config":config,"createdAt":"..."}
GET /api/kafka/connection?id=goldsky-main returns the latest revision, with revisions as a list of the same retained revision records.

### Explicit metadata inspection

POST /api/kafka/inspect
{"connection":"goldsky-main","revision":1,"operation":"inspect-main-1"}
Uses only that immutable configuration revision. A retry with the same operation returns the same retained inspection. A deliberate metadata refresh uses a new operation. Result:
{
 "id":"...","operation":"inspect-main-1","connection":"goldsky-main","connectionRevision":1,
 "configSha256":"...","observedAt":"...","client":client,
 "clusterId":"...","topicId":"...","topic":"events",
 "partitions":[{"partition":0,"low":"0","high":"120","end":"118","observedAt":"..."}]
}
GET /api/kafka/inspection?id= returns this exact record.
The provider is the official Confluent Python consumer/admin client. Metadata retains the broker cluster identity and native topic UUID, so a deleted/recreated topic cannot reuse an old capture identity. low/high are fresh native watermarks. end is the native READ_COMMITTED latest offset (last stable offset), not an invented dense row count or uncommitted high watermark.

### Capture preparation, run and cancel

POST /api/kafka/capture
{"inspection":"<inspection-id>","operation":"capture-main-1","ranges":[{"partition":0,"start":"0","end":"118"}]}
Requires explicit unique selected partitions and start/end within the retained inspected range. Result is capture below. Preparation does not contact a broker.

capture = {
 "id":"...","operation":"capture-main-1","inspection":"...","connection":"goldsky-main",
 "connectionRevision":1,"configSha256":"...","clusterId":"...","topicId":"...","topic":"events",
 "status":"PREPARED","revision":1,"records":0,"bytes":0,"retainedBytes":0,"boundaryRecords":0,"boundaryBytes":0,
 "ranges":[{"partition":0,"start":"0","end":"118","next":"0","status":"PREPARED","records":0,"bytes":0,"terminalEvidence":null}],
 "createdAt":"...","updatedAt":"...","error":null,"attempts":[]
}

GET /api/kafka/capture?id= returns capture plus the saved attempt records.
POST /api/kafka/run {"capture":"...","expectedRevision":1}
Returns HTTP 202 with the current capture after admitting its sole background native worker. Same capture is resumed from its retained checkpoints; an already running/completed operation is reconciled before another run.
POST /api/kafka/cancel {"capture":"..."}
Returns the current capture with CANCELLING while its existing consumer is closing. Checkpoints already committed remain durable.
Statuses: PREPARED, RUNNING, CANCELLING, CANCELLED, INTERRUPTED, COMPLETE, LIMIT_REACHED, SOURCE_GAP, SOURCE_CHANGED, SOURCE_CONFLICT, ERROR.
Reopening a workspace after its original process stopped converts unfinished RUNNING/CANCELLING to INTERRUPTED and retains the previous attempt.

Each run checks both Admin and actual Consumer cluster/topic identity and each unfinished range's retained-start retention bound, assigns explicit TopicPartitions, uses enable.auto.commit=false, enable.auto.offset.store=false, auto.offset.reset=error and isolation.level=read_committed. It never subscribes to or commits an existing customer's consumer group. Offsets may have compaction/transaction gaps. Completion requires a native observed record/EOF position reaching the selected end; an offset gap alone is not a missing-message finding. A record observed beyond the selected end may be retained as boundary evidence and is excluded from selected projection records. The same identity is cluster ID + topic UUID + partition + offset. Same-offset exact replay is idempotent; equal business content at distinct offsets remains distinct. Same identity with conflicting wire bytes is a retained source conflict. Final native metadata rechecks the original topic UUID; COMPLETE is emitted only after the native consumer closes. Previously completed partition ranges preserve their retained terminal evidence if another range later resumes after broker retention advances.

capture.bytes counts the full serialized original wire bytes for selected records. capture.boundaryBytes and boundaryRecords count retained boundary evidence. retainedBytes = bytes + boundaryBytes is the capture storage limit. Per-message maxMessageBytes applies to original payloadBytes (key/value/header bytes) for selected and boundary records alike.

Attempts are {"id":"...","startedAt":"...","endedAt":null,"status":"RUNNING","client":client,"error":null}. A running worker is polled at 250 ms. Persistence records each accepted batch and its next offsets together. Stop and process restart never silently skip to a newer retention low.

### Native message history

GET /api/kafka/messages?capture=<id>&offset=0&limit=50
returns {"capture":"...","offset":0,"limit":50,"total":120,"messages":[summary...]}.
Each summary contains id, sha256, clusterId, topicId, topic, partition, offset, timestampType, timestampMs, leaderEpoch, keyState, keyUtf8Preview, keyPreviewTruncated, keyBytes, valueBytes, headerCount, wireBytes, valueState, goldskyOperation and deleted. keyState is null, empty, utf8 or binary; keyUtf8Preview is at most 256 characters. Byte counts distinguish null from zero. Summary valueState is present or tombstone: list pages do not decode or parse all message values. Select the full /message endpoint for exact value bytes and JSON classification.
Page ordering is partition ascending then numeric offset; it does not claim global event ordering. Limits 1–200.
GET /api/kafka/message?id=<event-id> returns message including every original byte:
{
 "id":"...","sha256":"...","clusterId":"...","topicId":"...","topic":"events","partition":0,"offset":"14",
 "timestampType":"CREATE_TIME","timestampMs":"1791770000000","leaderEpoch":null,
 "keyBase64":"...","valueBase64":"...",
 "headers":[{"name":"dbz.op","valueBase64":"dQ=="}],
 "keyUtf8":"customer-42","valueState":"json","value":{},"valueJson":"{}","parseError":null,
 "goldskyOperation":"u","deleted":false
}
timestampType is NOT_AVAILABLE, CREATE_TIME or LOG_APPEND_TIME; timestampMs is null when unavailable. leaderEpoch is an integer or null. Duplicate header keys retain their order and bytes. valueState is json, tombstone, binary or invalid-json. A null value is a tombstone; b'' is not. Goldsky c/u/d comes from an unambiguous original dbz.op header. JSON numbers retain the original lexical value through the existing NDJSON JsonNumber implementation. valueJson contains the exact decoded JSON text for JSON values and null otherwise, so the browser can display numbers without JSON.parse/stringify coercion. Original Base64 remains the whitespace-preserving wire source.

### Retained projection into the original engine

POST /api/kafka/project
{
 "operation":"project-main-1",
 "captures":[{"id":"...","revision":7}],
 "view":"events",
 "decode":"json",
 "deletePolicy":"retain",
 "acceptIncomplete":false,
 "label":"Goldsky events"
}
view is events or latest-per-partition-key.
decode is json or bytes.
deletePolicy is retain, tombstone or tombstone-or-goldsky.
One projection selects 1–64 captures and at most 256 MiB of combined unique retained wire bytes. An active, source-changed or conflicting-source capture cannot be projected. Other incomplete capture selection requires acceptIncomplete=true and preserves exact coverage/state. The selected capture revisions and original message identities are frozen with the projection, so later capture continuation cannot alter an existing edition. Latest view chooses the largest offset for each exact topic UUID + partition + binary key; it does not invent cross-partition key ordering. A missing key must be resolved by choosing events.

Result:
{
 "id":"...","operation":"project-main-1","source":"<original-ndjson-source-id>",
 "sourceView":{},"selection":{...exact request...},"coverage":[...frozen capture records...],
 "records":120,"bytes":12345,"retainedBytes":23456,"excluded":0,"createdAt":"...",
 "defaultPlan":{...valid original stellar-forge.ndjson-mapping.v1 plan...}
}
GET /api/kafka/projection?id= returns the same record.
The derived NDJSON envelope contains eventId, partitionKeyId, clusterId, topicId, topic, partition, offset, offsetOrder, timestampType, timestampMs, leaderEpoch, keyBase64, valueBase64, headers, keyUtf8, valueState, value, parseError, goldskyOperation and deleted. Numeric metadata is encoded as exact decimal strings; offsetOrder is a 19-digit zero-padded offset usable by the original string sort. Original wire bytes remain the primary source.

Use the existing original mapping editor and /api/plan → /api/build → query/compare/merchant workflow on the returned source ID. State relates native builds to their Kafka projection by original build.source. The full original NDJSON UI is reused for those operations.

### Whole customer handoff

GET /api/kafka/export?build=<native-build-id>&projection=<projection-id> downloads kafka-project.zip containing the complete original native NDJSON project plus the selected Kafka connection references, native inspections, immutable source bytes, selected capture revisions and projection history. Manifest hashes bind all archive files and the original NDJSON source/plan/build identity.
POST /api/kafka/import accepts that raw ZIP and reconstructs the same retained source/projection and native original edition in a fresh private workspace. Reopening verifies original bytes and identities. Import does not contact a broker. Credential values are excluded; the receiver supplies the named private environment references to continue a capture.
The optional projection selector becomes required when several retained histories reconstruct identical source bytes. The seven root files are manifest.json, kafka.json, messages.jsonl, capture-revisions.jsonl, capture-members.jsonl, projection-events.jsonl and ndjson-project.zip. The transport limit is 6×256 MiB +32 MiB, with each JSONL≤256 MiB, metadata≤16 MiB, manifest≤16 KiB and the nested original project≤512 MiB. Before native reconstruction, receiving validates existing membership and checks the nested native manifest source-name SHA/build against the outer edition. The original receiver then owns all six-file validation and reconstruction.

The original /api/export and /api/dataset-export remain available for the standard native dataset outputs; /api/merchant remains the original seller/customer SDK operation. Kafka's whole-source archive is the adjacent source handoff.

## State

GET /api/state returns the original NDJSON state object plus:
kafka = {
 "schema":"stellar-forge.kafka-state.v1",
 "workspaceId":"<private-marker-UUID>",
 "client":client,
 "connections":[...latest connection revision records...],
 "inspections":[...retained inspections...],
 "captures":[...capture summaries including ranges and attempts...],
 "projections":[...projection records without sourceView/defaultPlan...],
 "activeCapture":null
}
History lists are newest first. Full source/inventory and defaultPlan are fetched with the projection/source routes; retained complete records are never replaced by list truncation.

# Kafka merchant workspaces

The Kafka merchant provider lets an agent complete the source-to-customer workflow
in the Kafka Application: inspect an exact topic, retain explicit partition
ranges, build an NDJSON dataset, compare editions and receive a complete merchant
package. The existing Kafka HTTP server owns the databases, native writer and
consumer. The browser, Node client and merchant tools all use that owner.

The source-owned provider ID is `kafka-workspaces`. Its 26 tools use
`merchant_kafka_`. [CLIENT.md](CLIENT.md) describes the complete Node client,
CLI and native route contract. [MERCHANT-DOWNLOAD.md](MERCHANT-DOWNLOAD.md)
covers the customer downloader, durable resume and local reopening.
[CONTRACT.md](CONTRACT.md) explains the retained
source, offsets, projection and archive semantics.

## Configure an existing Application

Open the Kafka Application and retain its private connection file. The client
accepts the original console URL file or Applications URL record. Keep that file
on its original operator host with mode 0600. The reader checks regular-file
identity, ownership and permissions; each operation authenticates the original
`/api/launch` and workspace/source binding.

Create a private host configuration, for example /private/kafka-connections.json:

~~~json
{
  "schema": "stellar-forge.kafka-merchant-connection.v1",
  "workspaces": {
    "events": {
      "label": "Merchant event stream",
      "connectionFile": "/private/applications/kafka/console-url.json",
      "inputs": {}
    }
  }
}
~~~

File paths appear only in host configuration. Tools choose declared workspace
and input aliases. Optional expectedWorkspaceId and expectedBindingSha256 pin
the actual original launch. A refreshed Applications URL may select the same
workspace on a new listener; an existing client retains its original workspace
path, UUID and source binding.

Declare complete receiving inputs under the selected workspace:

~~~json
{
  "received_project": {
    "path": "/private/receiving/kafka-project.zip",
    "kind": "kafka-project",
    "sha256": "REPLACE_WITH_THE_ACTUAL_COMPLETE_FILE_SHA256"
  }
}
~~~

Supported kinds are kafka-project, ndjson-project and ndjson. Add an input only
when its complete file exists and replace the SHA placeholder with the real hash.
The host configuration supports 32 workspaces and 64 inputs per workspace.

Create setup options with the intended directory and host configuration:

~~~json
{
  "directory": "/private/kafka-merchant",
  "connection": "/private/kafka-connections.json",
  "name": "Kafka merchant workspace"
}
~~~

Run the maintained registry commands:

~~~sh
starforge merchant-providers inspect kafka-workspaces
starforge merchant-providers init kafka-workspaces --options /private/kafka-setup.json
~~~

The initializer creates the original release store, private customer-export
directory and merchant configuration. Repeating the exact setup reopens its
existing configuration. One original setup lease serializes publication of the
complete prepared directory.

The returned configuration works with the maintained merchant-mcp HTTP or stdio
host and its existing authentication. An existing merchant may add
`kafkaWorkspaceConnection` pointing to the new host configuration while
preserving its five common configuration fields and other providers.

## Complete workflow

### Inspect and select the actual source

Call `merchant_kafka_workspaces`, then `merchant_kafka_inspect` with a selected
workspace alias. Inspection reports the actual workspace UUID and source binding
without exposing the private console token or local file paths.

`merchant_kafka_state` returns complete native state.
`merchant_kafka_configured_topics` lists saved exact-topic connection revisions.

Save a connection with `merchant_kafka_save_connection`, using its current
expectedRevision and a stable operation:

~~~json
{
  "workspace": "events",
  "connection": "orders",
  "expectedRevision": 0,
  "operation": "orders-settings-v1",
  "config": {
    "schema": "stellar-forge.kafka-connection.v1",
    "label": "Order events",
    "brokers": ["127.0.0.1:19092"],
    "topic": "order-events",
    "security": {"protocol": "PLAINTEXT"},
    "requestTimeoutSeconds": 30,
    "maxMessageBytes": 16777216,
    "maxCaptureBytes": 268435456,
    "maxCaptureRecords": 1000000
  }
}
~~~

Select the actual broker, topic and security settings for the host. TLS and SASL
settings refer to existing server environment variables. Credential values stay
in that original environment.

Call `merchant_kafka_inspect_connection` with the saved connection revision and
a stable inspection operation. Keep the returned inspection ID, actual cluster
ID, topic UUID, partition identities and committed low/end offsets.

### Retain explicit ranges

`merchant_kafka_prepare_capture` takes that inspection ID and ranges shaped as
`{"partition":0,"start":"0","end":"12"}`. Select actual observed offsets.
End offsets are exclusive. Every offset remains decimal text, including values
above JavaScript's safe integer range; each partition occurs once in the selection.

Use `merchant_kafka_run_capture` with the returned capture ID and expectedRevision.
The original consumer uses read_committed and direct partition assignment.
`merchant_kafka_wait_capture` returns the actual state after RUNNING/CANCELLING.
Cancelled, interrupted and limited captures retain their exact received coverage.

`merchant_kafka_cancel_capture` controls that original capture.
`merchant_kafka_resume_capture` uses its same ID and current revision.
Recover interrupted calls with the original operation and retained record IDs.

### Create a dataset edition

`merchant_kafka_messages` pages compact metadata and exact offsets.
`merchant_kafka_message` retains the complete original message JSON for file
receiving, preserving raw key/value bytes, ordered headers and tombstones.

`merchant_kafka_project` selects original capture IDs/revisions and these fields:

| Field | Choices |
| --- | --- |
| view | events; latest-per-partition-key |
| decode | json; bytes |
| deletePolicy | retain; tombstone; tombstone-or-goldsky |
| acceptIncomplete | Explicit boolean |
| operation | Stable original projection operation |
| label | Retained source edition label |

The original projector enforces topic identity, coverage and deletion rules and
creates the corresponding native NDJSON source. Save a complete native mapping
plan through `merchant_kafka_save_plan` using planJson text; build it with
`merchant_kafka_build` and the returned source/plan IDs.

`merchant_kafka_query` takes original scalar-string query parameters.
`merchant_kafka_compare` retains a full before/after comparison;
`merchant_kafka_changes` pages that saved change set.
`merchant_kafka_read` reopens connections, inspections, captures, projections,
sources and plans by their original identities.

### Receive complete files

`merchant_kafka_export` takes a stable operation, kind and exact selection:

| Kind | Selection | Complete file |
| --- | --- | --- |
| kafka-project | {build, projection?} | Kafka archive containing its native NDJSON project |
| ndjson-project | {build} | Native NDJSON project ZIP |
| dataset | {build} | Original dataset ZIP |
| changes | {id} | Complete comparison change NDJSON |
| merchant | {build, payment, origin, path} | Original merchant package ZIP |
| message | {id} | Full raw message JSON |
| state | {} | Full current state JSON |
| projection | {id} | Full retained projection JSON |
| record | {kind, id} | Connection, inspection, capture, source or plan JSON |
| query | {build, query} | Full original query JSON |

The merchant payment object, public origin and route use the native NDJSON
merchant contract. The original publisher prepares the package; customer checkout
and settlement use that package's existing workflow.

The export result contains the actual artifact, original source binding, complete
byte count and SHA-256. A customer can receive it with the installed command:

~~~sh
starforge kafka-merchant-download inspect \
  --url "$KAFKA_MCP_URL" --workspace "$KAFKA_WORKSPACE" --artifact "$KAFKA_ARTIFACT"

starforge kafka-merchant-download download \
  --url "$KAFKA_MCP_URL" --workspace "$KAFKA_WORKSPACE" --artifact "$KAFKA_ARTIFACT" \
  --manifest-sha256 "$KAFKA_MANIFEST_SHA256" --directory ./received-kafka-export

starforge kafka-merchant-download verify \
  --workspace "$KAFKA_WORKSPACE" --artifact "$KAFKA_ARTIFACT" \
  --manifest-sha256 "$KAFKA_MANIFEST_SHA256" --directory ./received-kafka-export
~~~

The inspect result supplies the actual manifest hash. The endpoint's bearer token
uses the existing MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN environment variable. Repeat the same download
selection and directory to resume its durable checkpoint. Local verification
reopens the completed manifest and file with the merchant stopped.

[MERCHANT-DOWNLOAD.md](MERCHANT-DOWNLOAD.md) includes source binding pins,
cancellation, the typed SDK and receiving each native file kind.

For an agent that consumes file chunks directly, use
`merchant_kafka_file_read`:

~~~json
{
  "workspace": "events",
  "artifact": "ACTUAL_RETURNED_ARTIFACT_ID",
  "expectedSha256": "ACTUAL_RETURNED_FILE_SHA256",
  "offset": 0,
  "limit": 65536
}
~~~

Keep each returned readId, expectedSha256 and nextOffset. Decode base64 chunks
to bytes in order. nextOffset:null completes the file. Verify its full received
size and SHA-256. Following a timeout, release or host restart, omit the expired
readId and reopen the same artifact at its original expectedSha256 and byte
offset. The read-only descriptor retains that exact file.

`merchant_kafka_file_release` releases a descriptor early.
`merchant_kafka_manifest` and `merchant_kafka_exports` inspect retained files
without contacting Kafka. Set includeFile:true on the manifest tool to receive its
exact retained manifest.json bytes, length and SHA-256; the customer downloader
pins its original manifest before receiving the payload. An incomplete export listing returns its original
operation and selection for recovery.

### Import and reopen

Declare the complete received file and actual SHA-256 under a host input alias.
`merchant_kafka_import` selects that alias in the intended receiver workspace.
Kafka imports perform the original full outer/inner archive validation. Native
project/source inputs use their original inherited routes. The client hashes and
transfers the same opened file and checks identity through the upload.

Reopen the original retained source, plan, build, capture and projection identities
in the receiver. Query its dataset against the source edition selected for that
customer.

## Exact numbers, large responses and recovery

Kafka offsets and timestamps stay decimal strings. The Node client represents
unsafe or noncanonical numeric JSON tokens as KafkaJsonNumber. Ordinary MCP JSON
uses `{"$kafkaNumber":"the original numeric token"}`; the native serializer
writes the original token as a number. Preserve this value instead of coercing it
to a Number. planJson accepts complete exact JSON text.

Native files stream byte for byte. A native result above 128 KiB is retained as
complete exact-number JSON, and its tool response returns the original file
manifest. A result above the configured in-memory JSON limit can be received
through the corresponding explicit state, record, projection or query export.

Before downloading, the merchant saves one immutable selection containing the
workspace binding, operation, kind and complete input. Its artifact ID is stable
for that workspace alias and operation. Changed selections under the same
operation are rejected; a new observation uses another operation.

The client writes an owned temporary file, validates the entire response length,
syncs it and links only a completed file to the final destination. A lost result
after publication reopens and hashes that same file before completing its
manifest. A transfer interrupted before publication resumes the same export
selection. The original Linux flock primitive serializes each export across
merchant processes. Retained metadata also tolerates its original temporary hard
link after a process interruption.

The shared RetainedFileReads owner receives the original read-only descriptor,
checks its complete SHA before its first range and serves large immutable files
without another full copy. Its four-read capacity and idle expiry apply.

Closing the provider cancels its own HTTP/checksum work and drains accepted
operations and descriptors. Applications continues to own the Kafka server.
A source capture is cancelled through its explicit tool. A native POST interrupted
after dispatch carries outcomeUnknown; reopen its same operation/record.

# Receive a Kafka merchant export

The merchant downloader saves a complete Kafka export on the receiving machine. It uses the merchant's existing MCP endpoint, keeps the exact native manifest, and resumes the same file after a connection loss or interruption. The SDK and CLI share the maintained merchant download engine.

Start with the workspace alias and artifact returned by a Kafka merchant export. The agent can create that export with `merchant_kafka_export`, or use the retained artifact returned for a large response or a complete message. The file remains associated with its original workspace UUID, source binding, export operation, content length and SHA-256.

The installed command is `starforge kafka-merchant-download`. The programmatic entry is the package's `./merchant/mcp/kafka/download` export. The repository entrypoint is `stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/kafka/merchant-download-cli.mjs`.

## Review and receive

Use the original HTTPS MCP address or its loopback HTTP address. Supply its bearer token through the existing environment variable `MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN`; `--token-env` selects a different variable name.

First inspect the selected artifact:

```sh
starforge kafka-merchant-download inspect \
  --url "$KAFKA_MCP_URL" \
  --workspace "$KAFKA_WORKSPACE" \
  --artifact "$KAFKA_ARTIFACT"
```

The JSON result includes the native manifest, the exact manifest SHA-256, the file's name and media type, total bytes, workspace UUID and source binding. It also gives the stable export operation. Use those values to select the intended source and file.

Receive the reviewed artifact into a private directory whose parent already exists:

```sh
starforge kafka-merchant-download download \
  --url "$KAFKA_MCP_URL" \
  --workspace "$KAFKA_WORKSPACE" \
  --artifact "$KAFKA_ARTIFACT" \
  --directory ./received-kafka-export \
  --manifest-sha256 "$KAFKA_MANIFEST_SHA256" \
  --workspace-id "$KAFKA_WORKSPACE_ID" \
  --binding-sha256 "$KAFKA_BINDING_SHA256"
```

The directory is created with private permissions. Progress is written to stderr after durable chunks; stdout contains the final JSON result. `--quiet` suppresses progress, and `--chunk-size` selects 1–196608 bytes per request.

The completed directory contains:

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `manifest.json` | The exact native manifest bytes received from the merchant. |
| `original.zip`, `original.json` or `changes.ndjson` | The complete original file named by that manifest. |
| `download-state/` | The original endpoint, manifest binding, durable byte checkpoint and local download lease. |

A file is published under its completed name only after its full bytes match the native SHA-256. An existing different file or manifest produces a conflict while preserving the saved contents.

## Resume the same transfer

Repeat the same download command, including the endpoint, workspace, artifact and directory. The engine checks the saved manifest, verifies the checkpointed prefix, and continues at the retained byte offset. It removes only a suffix that was written after the last durable checkpoint.

A remote read descriptor can expire or disappear when the merchant restarts. The downloader reopens the same artifact at the saved offset using its original file SHA-256. Keep the MCP address stable when restarting a local merchant. Changing the selected endpoint is a different receiving identity and the existing checkpoint will reject it.

Ctrl-C and SIGTERM cancel the current requests and drain the accepted local writes. The CLI keeps its signal handlers active until that drain ends. A later invocation continues the saved checkpoint. Exit codes are 0 for completion, 1 for an operation failure, 130 for an interrupt and 143 for SIGTERM.

To reopen and check the completed local download:

```sh
starforge kafka-merchant-download verify \
  --directory ./received-kafka-export \
  --workspace "$KAFKA_WORKSPACE" \
  --artifact "$KAFKA_ARTIFACT" \
  --manifest-sha256 "$KAFKA_MANIFEST_SHA256"
```

This command reads the existing local manifest, checkpoint and file. It reports the same source identifiers and exact file path after checking the complete length and SHA-256. It works with the merchant stopped and requires no token. Verification and resumed-prefix reads also accept cancellation.

1. **Save the connection.** Enter the actual bootstrap addresses and topic. Choose its security protocol and the names of the environment variables holding credentials or private TLS file paths. 3. **Prepare exact ranges.** Select partitions and review inclusive start/exclusive end offsets. Decimal offsets retain every digit. A prepared capture fixes its configuration revision, original inspection, topic identity and ranges.

4. **Run the capture.** The native consumer assigns the selected partitions directly and persists original events together with their next offsets. 5. **Review retained messages.** Inspect partition/offset identity, original key and value bytes, timestamps and ordered headers. UTF-8 view displays the original text, including exact numeric tokens. History pages carry compact offset/state/byte metadata and a key preview capped at 256 characters; selecting one event retrieves its full original value. 6. **Create a fixed source edition.** Select complete captures, or explicitly include their retained incomplete coverage. Choose every distinct event or the latest event for each exact binary key within a topic partition. Select JSON decoding or original bytes and the applicable deletion policy.

7. **Review the suggested mapping.** The complete existing NDJSON workspace opens with the source and suggested fields. Choose customer-visible columns and native filtering, sorting and key capabilities. Save the mapping, build the complete edition, query it and compare editions with the same keyed mapping.

8. **Deliver the complete project and merchant.** The original merchant section generates the seller package and customer SDK from the reviewed edition and actual payment terms. ## Source identity and ordering

An original event is identified by cluster ID, topic UUID, partition and offset. Equal event content at distinct offsets remains distinct. Exact replay of the same identity is idempotent; conflicting original bytes at the same identity become a retained source conflict.

The Goldsky sink documents at-least-once delivery and possible duplicates on retries. It publishes the original operation as the `dbz.op` header (`c`, `u` or `d`). This adapter retains those bytes and recognizes the operation only when its header value is unambiguous.

Kafka offsets can contain gaps after compaction or aborted transactions. A range's completion uses observed native record/EOF position reaching the selected end. Offsets are not interpreted as dense row counts. Records beyond the selected end can provide boundary evidence and stay outside the selected dataset records.

Latest-per-partition-key uses exact topic UUID, partition and binary key, choosing its greatest offset. It requires a key for every selected event. A partition-count change can redistribute keys; cross-partition business ordering remains an explicit downstream modeling decision.

JSON projections preserve original numeric lexical values through the existing NDJSON decoder. Avro and other binary values can be retained, inspected and delivered in bytes mode. JSON field mapping uses the JSON representation supplied by the producer.

## Recovery and complete exports

Each capture retains its immutable selection, status, revision, attempts, accepted message bytes and per-partition next offsets. An unfinished process becomes `INTERRUPTED` when the workspace reopens.

A source retention gap, a different cluster/topic identity or conflicting original event bytes is recorded in that capture. Inspect the current source and explicitly choose the appropriate following capture. Existing retained editions keep their original coverage and bytes.

A projection freezes selected capture revisions. Later continuation of those captures cannot rewrite that projection's source. The full Kafka export contains the original NDJSON project plus the selected source connection references, inspections, captured bytes, coverage and projection history with a file manifest. When several histories yield identical NDJSON source bytes, choose the required projection history in the export controls.

The complete handoff contains seven root files:

| File | Retained content |
| --- | --- |
| `manifest.json` | Exact projection/source/build identities and hashes of the other six members |
| `kafka.json` | Selected connection references, native inspections, operation journal, attempt metadata and fixed projection |
| `messages.jsonl` | Every original wire record required by that selected capture history, including boundary evidence |
| `capture-revisions.jsonl` | Complete checkpoint history through each selected capture revision |
| `capture-members.jsonl` | Original capture/message role and the revision that accepted it |
| `projection-events.jsonl` | Explicit inclusion/exclusion of each retained source event |
| `ndjson-project.zip` | Original six-file NDJSON source, mapping, native dataset and review |

The manifest is limited to 16 KiB, Kafka metadata to 16 MiB, each JSONL history file to 256 MiB and the nested original project to 512 MiB. The complete transport limit is 1,568 MiB. Actual valid source and mapping limits still govern reconstruction.

Import validates the complete wire history and projection, checks existing source/membership conflicts and joins the nested native source/build to the chosen outer edition before the original dataset receiver writes. The original engine then performs its full source/plan/build reconstruction, followed by the same retained Kafka history commit. If a process stops between those steps, the original operation names and source hashes reopen the same work.

The receiver supplies its own values for the saved environment variable references to continue broker access. Import and local dataset reconstruction use the retained project bytes.

    if len(data) != info.st_size or (after.st_size, after.st_mtime_ns, after.st_ctime_ns) != (info.st_size, info.st_mtime_ns, info.st_ctime_ns):
        raise InputError("The original private console connection changed while reading")
    try:
        url = data.decode("ascii")
    except UnicodeDecodeError as error:
        raise InputError("Choose the original private Kafka console connection file") from error
    if url.endswith("\n"):
        url = url[:-1]
    target = re.fullmatch(r"http://127\.0\.0\.1(?::([1-9][0-9]{0,4}))?/#([A-Za-z0-9_-]{40,64})", url)
    if target is None or not 1 <= int(target[1] or "80") <= 65535:
        raise InputError("Choose the original private loopback Kafka console connection")
    port, token = int(target[1] or "80"), target[2]

    def request(route, payload=None, limit=65536):
        # HTTPConnection connects directly to this exact loopback authority;
        # it neither follows redirects nor reads environment proxy settings.
        client = HTTPConnection("127.0.0.1", port, timeout=60)
        try:
            headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer " + token, "Accept": "application/json"}
            body = None
            if payload is not None:
                body = api_bytes(payload)
                headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
            client.request("GET" if payload is None else "POST", route, body=body, headers=headers)
            response = client.getresponse()
            retained = response.read(limit + 1)
            if response.status not in {200, 202}:
                raise InputError("The original Kafka console rejected the operation (HTTP " + str(response.status) + ")")
            if len(retained) > limit:
                raise InputError("The original Kafka console response exceeds the receiving limit")
            return load_json(retained)
        except HTTPException as error:
            raise InputError("The original Kafka console connection ended before receiving its response") from error
        finally:
            client.close()

    launch = request("/api/launch")
    expected = {"schema": "stellar-forge.kafka-workspace-launch.v1",
        "status": "KAFKA_WORKSPACE_READY", "workspace": binding["workspace"],
        "workspaceId": binding["workspaceId"], "bindingSha256": binding["sha256"],
        "console": url}
    if not isinstance(launch, dict) or any(launch.get(key) != value for key, value in expected.items()):
        raise InputError("The running console differs from this original Kafka workspace, Python or source")
    return request("/api/kafka/cancel", {"capture": capture}, 16 * 1024 * 1024)

    if args.command == "cancel":

        return 0
    binding = require_binding(args.workspace, args.expected_binding) if args.command == "serve" else None
    with Workspace(args.workspace, create=args.command == "init") as ws:

            binding = require_binding(str(ws.root), binding["sha256"])
        command = args.command
        if command in {"init", "list"}:
            result = ws.state()
        elif command in {"connection", "inspect", "capture", "project"}:
            callback = {"connection": ws.save_connection, "inspect": ws.inspect_connection,
                        "capture": ws.prepare_capture, "project": ws.project}[command]
            result = callback(input_json(args.file))
        elif command == "run":
            stopped = threading.Event()
            interruption = []
            def interrupt(number, _frame):
                if not interruption:
                    interruption.append(number)
                # Signal handlers never re-enter a SQLite transaction.
                stopped.set()
            old = {number: signal.signal(number, interrupt) for number in (signal.SIGINT, signal.SIGTERM)}
            try:
                result = ws.run_capture(args.capture, args.expected_revision, cancel_event=stopped)
            finally:
                for number, callback in old.items():
                    signal.signal(number, callback)
            emit(result)
            if interruption:
                return 130 if interruption[0] == signal.SIGINT else 143
            return 0 if result["status"] == "COMPLETE" else 2
        elif command == "messages":
            result = ws.messages(args.capture, args.offset, args.limit)
        elif command == "message":
            result = ws.message(args.id)
        elif command == "source":
            with Path(args.file).open("rb") as stream:

        elif command == "plan":
            result = ws.save_plan(input_json(args.file))
        elif command == "build":
            result = ws.build(args.source, args.plan)
        elif command == "query":
            result = ws.query(args.build, load_json(args.params))
        elif command == "compare":
            result = ws.compare(args.before, args.after)
        elif command == "changes":
            result = ws.comparison_page(args.comparison, args.offset, args.limit)
        elif command == "export":
            result = ws.export_kafka(args.build, Path(args.out).absolute(), args.projection)
        elif command == "dataset":
            result = ws.export_dataset(args.build, Path(args.out).absolute())
        elif command == "native-export":
            result = ws.export_packet(args.build, Path(args.out).absolute())
        elif command == "import":
            result = ws.import_kafka(Path(args.file))
        elif command == "native-import":
            result = ws.import_packet(Path(args.file))
        elif command == "merchant":
            result = ws.prepare_merchant(args.build, input_json(args.payment), args.origin, args.path, args.out)
        elif command == "serve":
            if not 0 <= args.port <= 65535:
                raise InputError("Port must be from 0 to 65535")
            server = OperatorServer(ws, args.port)
            previous = {}
            interrupted = []
            def terminate(number, _frame):
                if not interrupted:
                    interrupted.append(number)
                for kind in (signal.SIGINT, signal.SIGTERM):
                    signal.signal(kind, signal.SIG_IGN)
                raise KeyboardInterrupt
            for kind in (signal.SIGINT, signal.SIGTERM):
                previous[kind] = signal.signal(kind, terminate)
            try:
                with published_connection(args.connection_file, server.url) as connection:
                    server.launch = startup(server, binding, connection)
                    emit(server.launch if args.startup_format == "json" else {
                        "console": server.url, "workspace": str(ws.root),
                        **({"connectionFile": connection} if connection else {})})
                    server.serve_forever(poll_interval=0.2)
            except KeyboardInterrupt:
                pass
            finally:
                server.launch = None
                for kind in (signal.SIGINT, signal.SIGTERM):
                    signal.signal(kind, signal.SIG_IGN)
                try:
                    server.server_close()
                    ws.close()
                finally:
                    for kind, callback in previous.items():
                        signal.signal(kind, callback)
            return 0
        emit(result)
    return 0
